title: Webhook retry limit increased to 5 attempts
body: In Flowlytics v2.4, the webhook retry limit has been increased to 5 attempts. Previously, failed webhook deliveries were retried up to 3 times before being marked as permanently failed. This update includes a longer backoff tail between subsequent attempts to improve reliability during temporary network issues or downstream service outages.

title: Data sync latency reduced to 5 minutes
body: Flowlytics v2.4 introduces a major optimization to the ingestion pipeline, reducing data sync latency from 15 minutes down to 5 minutes. Event data now surfaces in your dashboards within 5 minutes, significantly improving real-time visibility into customer usage metrics and billing events. No configuration changes are required from your team to benefit from this performance update.

title: Legacy v1 export endpoints removed
body: Flowlytics version 2.4 removes the deprecated `/v1/export` endpoints. These endpoints are no longer operational and will return an error if called. All customers must migrate their integrations and data pipelines to the `/v2/export` endpoints to ensure continuous access to export functionality. Please review the version 2.4 migration guide for updated payload structures and authentication requirements.

title: Overage rate reduced to $0.08 per 1,000 events
body: The overage rate for Flowlytics has been reduced to $0.08 per 1,000 events. This change reflects a decrease of $0.02 from the previous rate of $0.10 per 1,000 events. The new rate applies to all customers, and the pricing model remains unchanged. The reduction aims to provide a more competitive offering for customers who exceed their allocated event limits.

title: Query timeout raised to 60 seconds
body: Flowlytics v2.4 increases the maximum query execution time to 60 seconds, extending the previous limit of 30 seconds. Long-running analytical and billing queries now have additional time to complete before aborting. If a query exceeds the new 60-second threshold, the platform terminates the process and returns the standard error code ERR_TIMEOUT_502. This adjustment accommodates more complex data aggregations and larger datasets across your workspace without requiring immediate query optimization.

title: Dashboard widget: funnel comparison
body:
Flowlytics v2.4 introduces the funnel comparison widget, allowing users to analyze two distinct segments side by side within a single dashboard view. This feature supports comparative analysis of conversion rates and drop-off points across different user cohorts simultaneously. 

To use this feature, add the widget from the dashboard customization menu, select your primary and secondary segments, and assign your desired funnel steps.

title: Fixed duplicate webhook deliveries
body: Flowlytics v2.4 addresses a race condition in the delivery worker that previously caused occasional duplicate webhook deliveries. This fix ensures each event payload is processed and sent exactly once by implementing a distributed locking mechanism across concurrent worker threads, resolving ingestion redundancy for downstream subscriber endpoints.

title: SCIM group sync
body: Flowlytics v2.4 introduces SCIM group synchronization capabilities. Administrators can now provision, update, and de-provision user groups directly from their Identity Provider. This update extends SCIM provisioning beyond individual user accounts, ensuring that group memberships automatically sync with Flowlytics access controls and permissions without manual intervention.

title: New error code ERR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH
body: Flowlytics v2.3 introduces a new error code, ERR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH. Previously, events with property types that conflicted with the existing schema were silently dropped by the ingestion pipeline. With this update, those events now return ERR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, enabling engineering teams to identify and debug data contract violations much faster without losing visibility into dropped payload streams.

title: Audit log export API
body: Flowlytics v2.3 introduces the audit log export API, enabling automated extraction of security and system events for compliance and monitoring workflows. Workspace administrators can now programmatically query audit records using standard authentication tokens. This addition supports filtering by timestamp and event category to streamline large-scale data ingestion into external security information and event management systems.

title: Snowflake integration GA
body: The Snowflake integration is now generally available in Flowlytics v2.3, leaving beta status with improved performance and reliability for production data pipelines. All existing beta configurations will automatically transition to the GA release without requiring manual intervention. Enterprise accounts can now leverage native synchronization without ingestion rate throttling, enabling direct querying and reporting across all connected billing workspaces.

title: API key scopes
body: Flowlytics v2.3 introduces API key scopes, allowing administrators to restrict access to specific resources when generating new credentials. Instead of granting blanket access across your entire account, you can now limit individual keys to exact operational domains such as analytics querying or billing management. This limits potential exposure if a credential is compromised. Existing API keys remain unaffected and retain full access until manually updated or replaced in your settings dashboard.

title: Batch size limit raised to 500 events
body: Flowlytics v2.3 increases the maximum ingestion batch size to 500 events per request, doubling the previous limit of 250 events. This update reduces network overhead and improves throughput for high-volume data pipelines sending payloads to the ingestion endpoint. API clients submitting batches exceeding 500 events will continue to receive a validation error. Ensure your SDK configurations and local batching logic are updated to take advantage of this increased threshold.

title: Fixed proration rounding error
body: In Flowlytics v2.3, a billing calculation bug affecting mid-cycle upgrades has been resolved. Previously, proration logic occasionally rounded upgrade charges up by one day, resulting in minor overcharges on customer invoices. The underlying decimal rounding rules have been updated to ensure accurate, day-precise calculations for all plan changes executed during an active billing cycle.

title: Usage metering dashboard
body: Flowlytics v2.3 introduces a real-time usage meter in the billing settings page. This component displays active event volume, current metered items, and projected overage charges without requiring a page refresh. Administrators can monitor consumption thresholds against plan limits to prevent unexpected billing interruptions. The meter updates automatically every sixty seconds and includes direct links to upgrade subscription tiers when usage approaches maximum capacity.

title: Improved ERR_TIMEOUT_502 diagnostics
body: In Flowlytics v2.3, gateway timeout responses associated with error code ERR_TIMEOUT_502 now include explicit diagnostic metadata to accelerate troubleshooting. When an upstream failure or slow execution triggers this gateway error, the returned payload now explicitly identifies the specific request_id alongside the internal processing stage that timed out. This additional context allows engineering and support teams to immediately isolate latency bottlenecks across distributed pipeline components without needing to manually correlate raw telemetry logs.

title: Webhook signature verification
body:
Flowlytics v2.2 introduces HMAC-SHA256 signature verification for all outbound webhooks to improve security and prevent request forgery. Each webhook delivery now includes a signature header containing the cryptographic hash of the payload, computed using your endpoint's secret key. 

To verify incoming requests, you must compute the HMAC-SHA256 hash of the raw request body using your webhook secret and compare it securely against the provided signature. Unverified payloads should be rejected immediately.

title: Dashboard public links
body: Flowlytics v2.2 introduces read-only public links for dashboards, enabling external sharing without requiring recipient authentication. Users with appropriate permissions can generate a secure URL from the dashboard settings menu. These links provide live access to underlying metrics while strictly preventing configuration changes or data exports. Public sharing can be revoked at any time by the dashboard owner or organization administrator, immediately invalidating the existing URL.

title: Custom metric formula functions
body:
Flowlytics v2.2 introduces two new formula functions for custom metrics: `PERCENTILE()` and `RATE()`. 

The `PERCENTILE(metric, p)` function computes the exact $p$-th percentile for a given metric stream over the evaluation window, where $p$ is a decimal value between $0.0$ and $1.0$. 

The `RATE(metric, interval)` function calculates the per-second rate of change for a metric across the specified time interval string, such as `1m` or `1h`. Both functions are now available in the metric builder for all enterprise tier accounts.

title: Parquet export format
body: Flowlytics version 2.2 introduces native support for writing data exports in the Apache Parquet format. This columnar storage format optimizes analytical query performance and reduces file sizes for large datasets exported from the platform. You can select Parquet as your preferred output format when configuring scheduled or on-demand data exports through the main dashboard.

title: Slack integration rebuilt
body: Flowlytics v2.2 introduces a complete rebuild of the Slack integration, transitioning the application to the new OAuth app model. This update improves security compliance, simplifies workspace authorization workflows, and aligns our Slack connectivity with current platform architecture standards. Existing integrations must be re-authenticated through the updated OAuth flow to maintain webhook delivery and alert configurations without interruption.

title: Fixed segment refresh stalling
body: Flowlytics v2.2 addresses a performance issue where segments containing more than 40 filters would stall during the hourly refresh cycle. This blockage prevented dependent metrics and billing runs from updating on schedule. The underlying query execution has been optimized to handle complex rule sets efficiently without hanging the worker threads.

title: JavaScript SDK v3
body: Flowlytics JavaScript SDK v3 introduces a rebuilt architecture utilizing native ES modules. This update reduces bundle size by 42% compared to v2.8, improving page load performance across all integrated applications. Async initialization is now standard, and legacy callback support has been deprecated. Developers can import individual analytics and billing modules independently to optimize payload size further.

title: Invoice PDF redesign
body: Flowlytics v2.2 introduces a redesigned invoice PDF that provides clearer line items for overage charges. The updated layout separates base subscription costs from metered usage overages, itemizing each usage tier and corresponding rate explicitly. This change improves billing transparency and resolves common audit discrepancies for enterprise accounts managing variable compute and storage allocations.

title: Rate limit headers added
body:
Starting with version 2.1, all Flowlytics API responses now include standard `X-RateLimit-*` headers to help you monitor your current request volume and consumption limits in real time. 

The response headers track your remaining capacity and reset intervals directly within the HTTP metadata, allowing your integrations to handle throttling thresholds programmatically before receiving rejection codes.

title: Cohort retention grids
body: Flowlytics v2.1 introduces cohort retention grids to track user engagement over specific time horizons. You can now analyze user retention patterns grouped by sign-up date, subscription tier, or custom event triggers. The grids display percentage-based retention rates across daily, weekly, and monthly intervals. This feature enables product and finance teams to identify churn inflection points, measure the long-term impact of onboarding changes, and correlate initial usage behavior with lifetime value more accurately.

title: Analyst role introduced
body: Flowlytics v2.1 introduces the Analyst role, positioned directly between the Admin and Viewer roles. This new permission level grants users full access to create, edit, and share custom analytics reports and billing dashboards without permitting administrative settings modifications or user management capabilities. Existing custom permission overrides remain unaffected by this update. Administrators can assign the Analyst role through the user management interface.

title: Tax exemption certificates
body: Flowlytics v2.1 introduces self-serve tax exemption certificate management for business customers. Administrators can now upload exemption documents directly through the billing portal. The system verifies uploaded files asynchronously. Once validated, automated tax calculations update immediately to remove applicable state and local taxes from future invoices.

title: Python SDK async client
body: Flowlytics v2.1 introduces an asyncio-native client in the Python SDK, allowing for non-blocking telemetry ingestion and billing event processing within asynchronous applications. The new asynchronous client shares the same method signatures as the synchronous version but utilizes `async/await` syntax for all network operations. This addition improves throughput and resource utilization for high-concurrency Python services integrating with the Flowlytics API.

title: Fixed ERR_INVALID_KEY on rotated keys
body: In Flowlytics v2.1, a bug involving key rotation has been resolved. Previously, API keys that had been recently rotated could incorrectly return the ERR_INVALID_KEY error for up to 60 seconds after the rotation event occurred. This issue has now been fixed to ensure immediate validation availability for newly rotated keys.

title: Segment refresh moved to hourly
body:
In Flowlytics v2.1, segment refresh intervals have been updated from every six hours to hourly. This change ensures that user segments update much faster across all active workspaces. 

No configuration changes are required from your team to enable this update. The faster refresh rate applies automatically to all existing and newly created segments.

title: ACH payments supported
body:
Flowlytics v2.1 introduces support for ACH payments for US customers. This update expands payment processing capabilities by allowing direct bank transfers alongside existing credit card options. 

US-based merchants can now configure ACH as an active checkout method through the billing dashboard. Transactions processed via ACH are subject to standard settlement timelines and verification procedures managed through our payment gateway integration.

title: Flowlytics v2 platform release
body:
Flowlytics v2.0 introduces general availability for the v2 API, featuring a redesigned event schema optimized for higher ingestion throughput and lower latency. 

Clients migrating from v1 must update their payload structures to comply with the updated schema definitions. Authentication mechanisms remain unchanged, but endpoint base paths now require the explicit `/v2/` prefix. Deprecated v1 endpoints will continue to receive critical bug fixes until the final sunset date.

title: Query engine rewrite
body: Flowlytics v2.0 introduces a complete rewrite of the query engine, replacing the v1 row store with a new columnar query engine. This architectural shift significantly improves aggregation performance and reduces memory consumption during large analytical workloads. Existing queries are fully compatible with v2.0, but customers should expect noticeably faster response times for all historical data retrieval and custom dashboard rendering.

title: Data retention controls
body: Flowlytics v2.0 introduces per-plan data retention controls in the workspace settings page. Workspace administrators can now configure specific retention periods based on their active subscription tier. This feature ensures compliance with internal data governance policies by automatically purging historical analytics data that exceeds the designated timeframe, helping organizations manage storage usage efficiently across different deployment environments.

title: SAML SSO
body: Flowlytics v2.0 introduces SAML-based single sign-on, available exclusively for Enterprise plans. This feature allows organizations to integrate Flowlytics with their existing identity providers to streamline user authentication and enforce centralized access policies. Administrators can configure custom SAML assertions and manage identity provider metadata directly from the security settings dashboard.

title: Usage-based billing
body: Flowlytics v2.0 transitions billing from a traditional seat-based model to usage-based metering. This update calculates platform charges dynamically according to active API calls and data volume processed within your billing cycle. Existing subscriptions will automatically migrate to the new structure at your next renewal date. You can review real-time consumption metrics and projected costs directly within the billing dashboard to monitor usage against your plan limits.

title: Deprecated v1 SDKs
body: With the release of Flowlytics v2.0, all v1 SDKs have officially entered maintenance mode. During this transition period, v1 SDKs will receive critical security patches and bug fixes only, with no new features planned. Users must migrate to the v2 SDK suite prior to the hard sunset date of December 31, 2026. After this date, all v1 endpoints will return error code 410 Gone, and support requests for v1 implementations will be closed. Refer to the v2 Migration Guide for step-by-step upgrade instructions.

title: Globex PrivateLink endpoints live
body: Flowlytics v2.3 introduces native support for Globex PrivateLink endpoints, now live in the us-east and eu-west regions. This integration allows enterprise customers to establish secure, direct connectivity between their infrastructure and Flowlytics without traversing the public internet. Network administrators can configure these endpoints directly from the platform dashboard to route billing and analytics data streams securely under strict compliance standards.
